blocks.text: Use a snapshot plus resumable event stream, a validator, a short ingest queue, an idempotent reducer, and a virtualized projection. Scheduling controls store and paint frequency; it never decides which authoritative comments survive.

Client architecture
- Comment stream manager (WebSocket/SSE)
- Buffer queue + batch scheduler
- Feed store (bounded list + dedupe)
- Virtualized list
- Moderation layer (mute/delete/report)

Delivery pipeline
- Real-time transport with cursor resume
- Monotonic sequence for ordering and gap detection
- Immutable event identity for replay deduplication
- Versioned moderation changes
- Optional server-owned slow mode or sampling policy

blocks.title: Snapshot-to-live projection
blocks.text: WS/SSE -> Buffer/Queue -> Scheduler -> CommentStore (bounded) -> VirtualizedList -> UI. Add a Moderation Filter between Store and UI.

steps.title: 1) Connect
steps.text: Open a WebSocket/SSE channel and load the latest N comments.

steps.title: 2) Buffer
steps.text: Push incoming events into a short queue instead of rendering immediately.

steps.title: 3) Batch apply
steps.text: Drain an accepted burst in one measured store transaction, preserving event identity, sequence, and gaps.

steps.title: 4) Render
steps.text: Render a virtualized list of the latest N items, applying moderation filters.

steps.title: 5) Recover
steps.text: Reconnect with backoff and fill gaps using cursor-based fetch.

blocks.title: Persist before deriving the viewport
blocks.text: Buffering + virtualization is the difference between smooth UX and a frozen page when chat spikes.

blocks.title: Stream and follow-mode boundaries
rows: Only schema-valid, deduplicated events may advance the contiguous cursor
Accepted comments can update pending count without moving the reader's anchor
Server tombstones preserve revision while personal hiding remains a projection

blocks.title: Gap-aware comment projection
blocks.text: Make the comment path explicit: snapshot and live frames pass validation, deduplication, ordering, moderation, and follow-mode placement before the visible list changes.

Ordering strategy
Use server-issued sequence for timeline order, event identity for replay deduplication, and an opaque cursor for resume. Timestamps remain display metadata, not the ordering contract.

Auto-scroll rules
If the user scrolls up, pause auto-scroll and show a badge; resume only when they return to the bottom.
Worked example: burst while the viewer reads older comments

The viewer has moved upward and disabled follow mode when a popular moment produces two hundred comments, including a later moderation removal. The UI must preserve reading position, process authority, and avoid one announcement per comment.

blocks.title: Scenario walkthrough
rows: Set follow mode paused and record the first visible anchor.
New data cannot steal reading position.
Deduplicate and batch accepted events into the normalized store.
A new-comments count appears instead of inserting above the anchor.
Apply a versioned tombstone to that comment identity.
The row becomes a compact removed state without collapsing the anchor.
Merge pending ordered IDs and clear the count after placement.
Scroll once to the live edge by explicit action.
Auto-follow resumes only by user intent.
